snippet.title: Eugene Sledge Hits the Beach at the Battle of Peleliu
snippet.description:
On 15 September 1944 Private Eugene Sledge and the rest of the K Company, 3rd Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment landed on the island of Peleliu.

During the run in to the beach, Private First Class Merrill Shelton offers Sledge a cigarette, which Sledge refuses. Shelton laughs, “Yeah, well, I’m makin’ you a bet. Before today’s over, you’ll be smokin’ every cigarette you can get your hands on.” Shelton's comment foreshadowed one of the bitterest battles of the Pacific in the Second World War.

snippet.title: Why Sparta Beat Athens - The Fall of the Empire - Peloponnesian War
snippet.description:

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on the Ancient Civilizations continues with an episode on how and why Sparta defeated Athens during the Peloponnesian War. Why did Athens lose the Peloponnesian War — and how did Sparta, a land power with limited naval experience, defeat the greatest maritime empire in the Greek world? This video breaks down the fall of Athens through five decisive factors: alliances, economics, geopolitics, internal politics, and public opinion. Athens began the war with wealth, fleets, and an empire built around the Delian League. But its harsh treatment of allies, the destruction of Melos, and the disastrous Sicilian Expedition weakened its image and drained its resources. Sparta, meanwhile, benefited from a more balanced alliance system, secure logistics, and eventually the one thing it needed most: Persian gold. With Persian backing, Sparta could build a fleet capable of challenging Athens at sea. After years of attrition, political coups, overextension, and strategic missteps, Athens finally lost control of its grain supply after Aegospotamoi. The result was surrender, occupation, and the rise of the Thirty Tyrants. This is the story of how Athens lost its empire — and how Sparta won the Peloponnesian War.

snippet.title: When Britain Built 40 Battleships in 10 Years
snippet.description:
Buy a Battle of Jutland Poster: https://www.historigraph.media/store
Support the videos on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/historigraph

On May 31, 1916, the two most powerful navies on Earth clashed in the North Sea in the greatest naval battle in history: The Battle of Jutland.

This video explores the furious, decade-long shipbuilding race that made this epic WWI showdown possible. Discover how Germany’s Kaiser Wilhelm II and Admiral Tirpitz challenged British naval dominance, and how the radical launch of HMS Dreadnought in 1906 revolutionized warfare overnight. We break down the fatal clash of design philosophies—British speed and firepower vs. German armour and survivability—and look at how Britain ultimately out-produced the German Empire by turning on its "ship printer."

0:00 -  From Friends to Enemies
4:35 - The Dreadnought Race
8:40 - Britain Turns the Ship Printer On 

Principal Sources:
V.E Tarrant, Jutland: The German Perspective
N. A. M. Rodger, The Price of Victory: A Naval History of Britain 1815-1945 
Robert Massie, Dreadnought

snippet.description:
Join the celebration: https://wo.ws/4gAGOGV Use the code USA250, whether you’re new or a returning player, you’ll get a massive pile of rewards, including the premium ships USS Albany and Smith for free, seven days of premium account access!

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on medieval history and history of Britain continues with episode 4 of our coverage of the Viking invasion of Britain, as we cover Edward the Elder's reconquest of the Danelaw. Alfred the Great saved Wessex from the Vikings, but his son Edward the Elder wanted more than survival. This episode follows the king who turned defense into conquest and pushed the Anglo-Saxon world toward the creation of England. After Alfred’s death, Edward faced a dangerous succession crisis as his cousin Æthelwold claimed the throne and sought Viking support from York, Essex, and East Anglia. The revolt ended in blood at Holme, but the Viking threat did not disappear. Edward and his Mercian allies then struck back. At Tettenhall in 910, the kings of York were destroyed, opening the way for a systematic campaign against the Danelaw. Working with his sister Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, Edward built fortresses, seized borderlands, crushed East Anglia, and captured key towns including Derby, Stamford, Nottingham, and Leicester. But victory came with a ruthless political move: Edward absorbed Mercia and became the most powerful ruler south of the Humber. From Ragnall’s rise in York to Edward’s fatal campaign at Chester, this is the story of conquest, family rivalry, Viking collapse, and the king who prepared the road for Æthelstan, the first ruler to claim all England after decades of war and shifting royal loyalties.

snippet.title: 1500 Years of Russian History in 30 Minutes
snippet.description:
Russia is the largest country on Earth. But its history is even bigger.

From Viking rulers and Mongol invasions to tsars, revolutions, world wars, and the Soviet Union, Russia has survived things that would have destroyed most countries. At one point, a single Soviet officer may have prevented World War III and saved millions of lives.

This is the story of how Russia became Russia, over 1,100 years of history in just 30 minutes.

snippet.title: Captain Andrew "Ack Ack" Haldane's Final Moments on Peleliu #thewarofficepodcast #history #ww2
snippet.description:
Captain Andrew "Ack Ack" Haldane, commander of K Company, 3rd Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, led his company from the front. On October 12, 1944, he volunteered himself to assess the area of Hill 140 for where to place the company's machine guns and mortars. As he was looking over the edge of a ridge, Haldane was killed by a Japanese sniper. The men of K Company were devastated by his death.
